---
title: "Datasets"
---

One entry per dataset configured in `config/` (the public ones; the app links here from its
Design and model tab, to the entry whose heading is the dataset id in lowercase). Each entry
records what the dataset is, how it is modelled, and what to know before trusting it. The
formulas and numbers come from the database (`dataset_design`, `variance_summary`); the
reasons come from the config comments and the findings in [Methods](methods.qmd). Per-timepoint
subsets (for example `ANEMONES_DAY1`) have no design of their own: they use their parent's, so
they link to the parent's entry.

## Reading the models {#reading-the-models}

Every dataset with a `design:` block gets the same two models (`R/lib/design.R`,
`R/targets/variance.R`).

- **`cell`.** One factor for group × timepoint (time alone, or group alone, when the dataset has
  only one of them). In the differential expression model the formula is `~0 + cell + ...`, so
  each coefficient is the mean expression of one cell and every question is a difference of cell
  means. This handles a group sampled at fewer timepoints than the others without special cases.
- **Variance model** (variancePartition, ML). Asks how much of each gene's variance each term
  explains; it tests nothing. Categorical variables are random effects, numeric covariates are
  fixed and standardized. *Between patients* is the patient term plus person-level variables
  (group, sex, age); *time* is time plus group × time; *residual* is change within a person that
  is not shared by time, plus noise. A variable with few levels gives a noisy variance estimate
  that is often exactly 0: read a 0 as "not distinguishable here", not "no effect".
- **Differential expression model** (dream, REML). For a time course: each later timepoint
  against the first, within each group, plus a joint test per group, with a patient random
  intercept so that samples from one person are not treated as independent. A covariate that is
  constant within a person (sex) is absorbed by that term; it is not cancelled exactly when
  people contribute to different cells. Cross-sectional datasets compare groups pairwise.
- **Technical covariates** (`vp_covariates`, or a control-probe `control_factor`) go into the
  variance model only.

Shares quoted below are variance-weighted over the genes the factor methods see (about 8,000):
between patients / time / residual.

## ANEMONES {#anemones}

ANEMONES (GSE236713), array, 447 samples from 194 patients; subsets `ANEMONES_DAY1`, `_DAY2`,
`_DAY5`, `_DISCHARGE`.

| Cells (samples / patients) | Day 1 | Day 2 | Day 5 | Discharge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sepsis | 125 / 124 | 93 / 93 | 69 / 69 | 37 / 37 |
| SIRS | 39 / 38 | 31 / 31 | 15 / 15 | 8 / 8 |
| Control | 30 / 30 | - | - | - |

The design is ragged: controls exist only at Day 1. A `disease * timepoint` model would contain
interaction terms for Control at later days that have no data; the cell-means model has none
and fits the same means where data exist. Control gets no time contrasts (one timepoint).

- **Variance model:** `~(1|patient_id) + (1|timepoint) + (1|disease) + (1|disease:timepoint) +
  (1|sex) + control_factor`.
- **DE model:** `~0 + cell + (1|patient_id) + control_factor`.
- **`control_factor`** is the first principal component of the array's positive control probes
  (96 ERCC, 10 Agilent E1A spike-ins and other controls; 72% of their variation). The deposited
  values have no between-sample normalization, and the sample-mean shift follows these controls
  (rho 0.92), not leukocyte composition. Shifting each sample by a control offset over-corrected
  (the controls move about twice as much as genes; sex agreement fell from 0.99 to 0.94), so the
  PC enters as a covariate instead.
- **Result:** 34% between patients, 1.7% time, 31% residual, plus a technical share (the control
  factor). Time effects are real for individual genes (7,134 genes at FDR < 5% for Sepsis, Discharge
  against Day 1) but small as a share of variance.
- **Quality:** sex agreement 0.99; 4 subjects have discordant sex annotations and stay in.

## CORTICUS {#corticus}

CORTICUS (GSE106878), array, 94 samples from 47 patients, each sampled at `Pre` and
`Post(24h)`; subsets `CORTICUS_PRE`, `CORTICUS_POST24H`. No group.

- **Variance model:** patient, timepoint, sex (random), age (fixed). **DE:** `~0 + cell +
  (1|patient_id)`, one contrast (Post against Pre).
- `time_order` is required because `Post(24h)` sorts before `Pre`. Treatment, responder and
  28-day survival are left out of the models because they can mediate the time effect.
- The array has no control probes; probes the annotation marks as matching no transcript stand in
  as a technical reference for the composition check.
- **Result:** 56% between patients, 3.5% time, 40% residual. PC1 tracks the neutrophil-lymphocyte
  score (rho -0.60).

## EARLI {#earli}

EARLI, RNA-seq, 189 samples, cross-sectional (one per person). Groups: `lca_label`
(Hyper- or Hypo-inflammatory subphenotype); covariates sex and age.

- No subject or time, so there is no between-patient term: the variance model is group, sex,
  age and residual, and the DE model compares the two subphenotypes.
- **Result:** 94% residual. The subphenotype carries about 5% of the variance.

## GSE110487 {#gse110487}

GSE110487, RNA-seq, 62 samples from 31 patients at `T1` and `T2`; subsets `GSE110487_T1`,
`GSE110487_T2`. No group or covariates (the only other column, response to treatment, is left
out).

- **Result:** 43% between patients, 1.2% time, 56% residual. PC1 is strongly the
  neutrophil-lymphocyte axis (rho -0.83), and that score is 61% patient-level: leukocyte
  composition is largely a stable person trait here.

## GSE13904 {#gse13904}

GSE13904, array, 227 samples from 186 patients at `day1` and `day3`; 41 patients have both,
145 only one. Subsets `GSE13904_DAY1`, `GSE13904_DAY3`.

- **Group:** `clinical_status`, taken at each subject's **first** timepoint
  (`group_at_first_time`), because a patient's status changes within person for 17 of the 41
  sampled twice (for example Septic Shock to SIRS resolved).
- No sex or age columns. Affymetrix hybridization spike-ins serve as the technical reference.
- **Result:** 59% between patients, 1.8% time, 39% residual. 98% of the per-gene fits are
  singular (a variance component estimated at exactly 0), and 145 of the 186 patients have a single
  sample, so per-gene shares are noisier here than in datasets where everyone is sampled twice.

## GSE273700 {#gse273700}

GSE273700, RNA-seq, 104 samples from 52 patients, each at `Day1` and `Day8`; subsets
`GSE273700_DAY1`, `GSE273700_DAY8`. No group or covariates.

- **Result:** 39% between patients, 2% time, 59% residual. PC1 is the neutrophil-lymphocyte axis
  (|rho| 0.90).

## GSE54514 {#gse54514}

GSE54514, array, 163 samples; timepoint `day` 1-5 (modelled as categorical), person id `group_id`
(for example `HC_1`); group `disease_status` (healthy, sepsis survivor, sepsis nonsurvivor);
covariates sex and age. Healthy controls are sampled at day 1 and day 5 only; patients across the
range. Subsets `GSE54514_DAY1` to `_DAY5`.

- **Data quality: this dataset's sample annotations do not match its arrays.** Sex inferred from
  chrY and XIST genes agrees with the recorded sex for only 50% of samples, and samples of one
  `group_id` disagree on sex in 35 of 54 subjects. It stays in the pipeline and the app, flagged,
  but its subject and time results are not interpretable as person-level results.
- **Result:** 7% between patients, 10% time, 83% residual: the near-absence of a stable
  between-patient share is consistent with the "subjects" not being real individuals.

## GSE95233 {#gse95233}

GSE95233, array, 102 samples from 51 patients at `D01`, `D02`, `D03` (22 healthy-control
samples with a missing timepoint are dropped). Covariates sex and age; the recorded sex `H`
(homme) is recoded to `M` (all four samples show the male XIST/chrY pattern). Subsets
`GSE95233_D01`, `_D02`, `_D03`.

- **Result:** 38% between patients, 4.2% time (the largest time share among the well-formed
  designs), 58% residual. Sex agreement 0.98 (one patient discordant).

## MARS {#mars}

MARS (GSE65682), array, 802 samples, cross-sectional. Group `healthy_control` (42 healthy
against 760 patients); covariates sex and age. There is no subject or time column (the title
identifiers are not repeated measures). No between-patient term; 75% residual.

## dilgom {#dilgom}

dilgom (E-TABM-1036), array, 518 samples, a healthy reference cohort, cross-sectional. Group
`age_band` (five levels); covariate sex; one DE contrast (65-74 against 25-34). 97% residual.

## hfgp-500fg {#hfgp-500fg}

hfgp-500fg (GSE134080), RNA-seq, 100 samples, a healthy reference cohort, cross-sectional.
Group sex, covariate age. It is a positive control: the top sex-differential genes should be on
chromosome Y. Sex agreement 1.0. Whether a healthy cohort belongs in a sepsis analysis is an
open scope question recorded in its config.

## SHIP-TREND {#ship-trend}

SHIP-TREND (GSE36382), array, 991 healthy samples. Its phenotype data is access restricted, so
there is no sample metadata: it gets factor fits but no design, variance or composition analysis.
It is the largest dataset (8,000 genes × 991 samples) and sizes the controllers' memory.

## gains {#gains}

gains: four pooled ArrayExpress accessions (E-MTAB-4421, 4451, 5273, 5274), array, no timepoint.
**Not in the pipeline**: its preprocessing script is a stub until it is decided whether to pool
the four accessions.
